case.why: Job ids count up, so they are guessable. Only the owner or the token holder may read a job. And a job left 'running' by a crash blocks its project's next sync forever.

swept 1 unfinished job(s); state now 'failed': The server stopped before this finished. Start it again.

zip not accepted: 400 - 'Requirements' artifacts do not accept .zip archives.
not a zip: 400 - '__archive_1.zip' is not a valid .zip archive.
index out of range: 400 - File index 7 is out of range.
oversized file: 413 - 'big.txt' exceeds the 0 MB per-file limit.
pasted text for code: 400 - 'Code' artifacts cannot be provided as pasted text.
connected source, no login: 401 - Sign in to run an analysis from a connected source.

observed: sync: Version 2: 1 source(s) refreshed, 1 configuration(s) re-run.

pipeline log: ['Carried 1 link(s) from the last run into classification']; 'no match' warnings: 0

case.feature: Link pinning / saving a result that carries no pairs
case.why: An older saved result, or another client, does not send the pairs. Reading that as 'this run linked nothing' would delete the pins a later sync depends on.
case.preconditions: A configuration with 2 stored pins, from a saved New Analysis
case.input: Run the same New Analysis twice more into the same configuration, changing only the result before saving: once with the 'element_links' field removed, once with it sent as an empty list
case.expected: All three runs are filed under one configuration. Field removed: the save succeeds and the 2 pins are left untouched. Empty list sent: the pins are cleared, because that run said it linked nothing

tests.description: A result that does not mention the pairs changes nothing; only an explicit empty list clears them.
observed: saved with no 'element_links' field: 201, pins now 2

case.feature: Link pinning / pairs stay with the saving user's configuration
case.why: The pairs now arrive from the browser. They must only ever be stored against the configuration of the project the caller owns.
case.preconditions: User A has a saved New Analysis with 2 pins. User B is a different signed-in user
case.input: B saves a result carrying pairs into B's own project, with the same settings as A. Then B posts that result to A's project
case.expected: B's own configuration gets its 2 pins. The post to A's project is refused with 404. A's pins are 2 before and after both

tests.description: Pairs sent with a save are stored for the saver's own project and nowhere else.
observed: A's pins before: 2; after B's own save and B's post to A's project: 2
B's own configuration (a different one): 2 pins

case.feature: Sync / a kind shared by two pairs
case.why: Requirements feed two pairs. After syncing one, the other is looking at old requirements and must say so, then catch up on request.
case.preconditions: One project with requirements->code and requirements->architecture_document, both run on the same requirements
case.input: Sync the code pair with changed requirements. Read the pairs. Then sync the document pair with no new files and no force
case.expected: After the first sync only the document pair is out of date. Its sync starts without force, re-runs 1 configuration, and afterwards neither pair is out of date

tests.description: A pair whose shared source moved on is flagged, and a plain sync brings it up to date.

document pair sync: started=True, Version 4: 0 source(s) refreshed, 1 configuration(s) re-run.
after syncing the document pair: {'code': False, 'architecture_document': False}

case.why: A sync with nothing to do must not create an empty version or spend model calls; but re-running on purpose must still be possible.
case.preconditions: A saved requirements->code run; nothing has changed since
case.input: Sync the pair without force, then with force=true
case.expected: Without force: started=false, 'already up to date', still 1 version. With force: a job runs and creates version 2 with the same 3 links (+0 -0)

observed: no force: started=False, 'Everything is already up to date. Nothing was fetched.', versions [(1, 1)]
force: Version 2: 0 source(s) refreshed, 1 configuration(s) re-run.; config 58: ok, 3 links (+0 -0)

case.why: Each refusal protects something: a pair with nothing to restore from, files that are no longer there, and two syncs writing the same graph at once.
case.input: Sync: a pair never run; a replacement for an unknown source; a replacement naming an expired upload; an empty body; and a sync while another sync job is unfinished
case.expected: 409, 400, 410, 422 and 409 in that order, each with a message saying what is wrong; no new version created by any of them

tests.description: A sync that cannot be done is refused up front with a reason.
observed: pair never run: 409 - This project has no saved run from requirements to architecture with stored artifacts, so there is nothing to
unknown source: 400 - Source 999999 cannot have its files uploaded.
expired upload: 410 - Those uploaded files are no longer waiting - staged uploads are cleared after a while. Upload them again.
empty body: 422 - source_kind and target_kind are required
already syncing: 409 - This project is already being synced by job 48.

case.feature: Sync / broken links through the API

case.why: Every trace link is a parsed model reply. A reply read the wrong way is a wrong link shown to the user.
case.input: Well-formed replies: <trace>yes</trace>, <trace>NO</trace>, a <think> block saying yes followed by <trace>no</trace>, and a reply with an <explanation>
case.expected: yes -> linked, NO -> not linked, the <think> block is ignored, and the explanation text is returned

tests.description: A reply that follows the prompt's format is read from its tags, whatever else it says.
observed: simple: {'<trace>yes</trace>': True, '<trace>NO</trace>': False, '<think>yes, this could match</think>\n<trace>no</trace>': False, 'Reasoning: yes and no.\n<trace>no</trace>': False}
reasoning: {'<trace>yes</trace>': True, '<trace>NO</trace>': False, '<think>yes, this could match</think>\n<trace>no</trace>': False, 'Reasoning: yes and no.\n<trace>no</trace>': False}
reasoning with explanation: (True, 'The method checks the passphrase.')

case.why: Models sometimes omit the tag. Reading 'yes' inside another word turns a clear 'no' into a false trace link.
case.input: Replies with no <trace> tag: 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.' and 'No - that was removed yesterday.'
case.expected: Both read as not linked, by both classifiers

tests.description: A reply without the tag that plainly says no must not become a link.
tests.failure:
AssertionError: 4 of 4 replies saying 'No' were read as a link
assert not [('simple', 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.'), ('simple', 'No - that was removed yesterday.'), ('reasoning', 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.'), ('reasoning', 'No - that was removed yesterday.')]
observed: simple: 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.' -> linked
simple: 'No - that was removed yesterday.' -> linked
reasoning: 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.' -> linked
reasoning: 'No - that was removed yesterday.' -> linked

wrong purpose -> That sign-in link is not valid.
expired -> That sign-in link has expired. Try connecting again.

case.why: A repository tarball is unpacked onto the server. Entries with '..' or symlinks are how an archive escapes its folder.

case.expected: Only src/A.java is written, without the 'repo-abc' wrapper folder; nothing outside the destination

tests.description: Only plain files inside the repository are unpacked, with GitHub's wrapper folder dropped.

case.why: Users paste whatever GitHub shows them. Each form must resolve to the same repository, and junk must be refused before any request.

case.why: GitHub tokens are stored in the database. They must not be readable there, and a changed key must fail loudly, not return garbage.

observed: with a different key: A stored access token could not be read. This happens when secret_key changes; the connection has to be made again.

case.expected: UC1->login, UC2->logout, UC3->borrow; UC4 unimplemented; with expansion depth 1, a strong link to logout() also reaches clear(), which it calls

case.expected: 2 compared components with those interfaces and their operations in the text; 2 interfaces, not compared

case.why: Expansion multiplies links. It must stop at the depth asked for and must not grow weak links into more weak links.

case.expected: Depth 1: strong link reaches b only. Depth 2: reaches b and c with decayed confidence. The weak link is never expanded

case.expected: The same 16-character key both times
